context.history: The funeral's emptiness contrasts with the crowds at the parties. Henry Gatz's pride in his son's wealth and the boyhood 'schedule' echo Benjamin Franklin's famous plan of self-improvement in his Autobiography, a founding text of the American self-made man.

segments.script: The funeral's emptiness contrasts with the crowds at the parties. Henry Gatz's pride in his son's wealth and the boyhood 'schedule' echo Benjamin Franklin's famous plan of self-improvement in his Autobiography, a founding text of the American self-made man. Nick moves from Gatsby's story to America's: the Dutch sailors' 'fresh, green breast of the new world' links Gatsby's longing to the nation's founding dream, and the last sentence makes the struggle against the past universal. Characterization: Almost no one comes to Gatsby's funeral; his father arrives. Structure: Nick's final judgment of Tom and Daisy and his reflection on the Dutch sailors. Symbolism: the green light and the "fresh, green breast of the new world." Watch for the green light: The light at the end of Daisy's dock: Gatsby's dream, distant and unreachable, and finally the "orgiastic future" that recedes before everyone. In this chapter: “and untrue. When Michaelis’s testimony at the inquest brought to light Wilson’s suspicions of his wife I thought the whole tale would” (Chapter IX, paragraph 2).

segments.activity: Model the close reading of the anchor quotation using the written think-aloud below.
segments.script: First, meaning. I read “They were careless people, Tom and Daisy—they smashed up things and creatures and then retreated back into their money” slowly and put it in my own words: Nick says Tom and Daisy smashed up things and people and then retreated into their money. Next, craft. I notice the violent verb "smashed" next to "creatures," which treats people like objects. The strongest word is “careless”: it is a mild word for terrible harm, which shows how easily the rich ignore consequences. Then, effect. What does Nick mean by calling Tom and Daisy "careless"? My answer: By calling Tom and Daisy "careless," Nick means their money lets them smash things and people and retreat; he condemns the class that let Gatsby, Myrtle and Wilson die.
